> It's the CI job that checks the OpenSpec files are well-formed (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:86-89`). It only reads markdown and never runs the app.
> 
> Each part of the command:
> 
> - **`npx -y`** downloads and runs the package without installing it. `-y` skips the "install this package?" prompt.
> - **`@fission-ai/openspec@1.14.3`** is the OpenSpec CLI, pinned to the same version you have locally (`openspec --version` → 1.14.3).
> - **`validate --all`** checks every spec in `openspec/specs/` and every change in `openspec/changes/`. Right now the changes are `configuration-de-deploiement`, `fermeture-de-session`, `gestion-des-outils`, `liste-de-contacts`, `photo-des-outils` and `schemas-initiaux`.
> - **`--no-interactive`** turns off prompts so it can't hang waiting for input in CI.
> - **`OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY: 0`** (the step's `env`) turns off OpenSpec's usage telemetry.
> 
> **What it checks:** the structure of each spec and change. That means requirements written with `SHALL`/`MUST`, each requirement having at least one `#### Scenario:`, delta specs using sections like `## ADDED Requirements`, and so on. These rules come from how OpenSpec generally works, not from this repo. The command should exit non-zero on an error, which fails the job. I haven't checked that exit behaviour in this repo.
> 
> **What it probably skips:** the `archive/` folder. `validate` has a separate `--archived` flag for archived changes, so `--all` likely doesn't include them. That's a guess from the help text; I haven't tested it.
> 
> To run the same check locally, use `openspec validate --all --no-interactive`. Adding `--strict` would make the rules stricter.
